description:
Build the scripted-local runner harness that drives the v2 helper through its JSON-RPC socket and asserts the rows from N-008 §§8–14 marked `type: scripted-local`. First milestone is the 18-row smoke suite (N-008 §22) executing end-to-end on M1.

Responsibilities (binding):
- Open the helper IPC socket per N-007 §1 transport (UDS at $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/cove-screen-recorder/engine.sock on Linux/macOS; named pipe on Windows). Length-prefixed JSON-RPC 2.0, 1 MiB frame cap.
- Drive the JSON-RPC method namespace from N-007 §2: capture.{listSources,requestSession,startStream,pauseStream,resumeStream,stopSession,setRegion,setFramerateHint,setCursorMode}; replay.{save,snapshot_release,recoverable_sessions,discard_recovered_session,restore_recovered_session,export_start,export_cancel}; engine.{version,health,setLogLevel,shutdown,diagnosticsBundlePath}.
- Subscribe to and record events: capture.{sessionReady,formatChanged,streamPaused,streamResumed,sessionLost,diagnostics}; encoder.{probeResult,selected,fallbackEngaged,runtimeError,backPressure,diagnostics}; replay.{segmentDiagnostics,recoveryAvailable,snapshotPinned,snapshotReleased}; export.{queued,started,progress,stalled,completed,failed,cancelled,rejected}; engine.{ready,shutdownStarted,logLine,stateChanged,crashed}. Renderer-events.jsonl (N-008 §7) is produced from this stream.
- Implement the ffprobe/mediainfo recipes from N-008 §20 as reusable assertions: duration; declared fps; frame count; duplicated-PTS detection (≤ 1 / 60 s); real cadence (mean / 95p / 99p inter-PTS interval); faststart (mediainfo IsStreamable + moov-precedes-mdat one-liner); codec (h264 only for v2.0.0 GA); GOP / fragment structure on segment files.
- Implement the universal pass/fail thresholds from N-008 §6 as reusable predicates: capture drop tiers per resolution × encoder; encoder drop tiers; no-fake-duplicated-frames; cadence; duration; save latency (≤ 250 ms + fragment latency, worst case ≈ 2.25 s); HUD ≥ 1 Hz during SAVING (sampled from event arrival cadence); exactly-one terminal event per exportId; encoder.fallbackEngaged ≤ 1/session; no mid-session encoder switching; Linux re-encode = libx264 only (assert ffmpeg invocation); 5 s after shutdown pgrep zero rows for cove-replay-engine|ffmpeg|pactl; pactl never spawned in any process tree under the helper PID; restart loop bounded ≤ 3 in 60 s; helper sha256 / protocol mismatch refuses boot.
- Collect the evidence bundle per N-008 §7 per row: engine.diagnosticsBundle.zip; capture.json; encoder.json; segments.json; export.json per exportId; out.mp4; out.mp4.ffprobe.json; out.mp4.mediainfo.json; pre_pgrep.txt and post_pgrep.txt; renderer-events.jsonl; dmesg.tail (journalctl --since '<run start>'). Verify the diagnostics-bundle redaction rule from N-007 §16 (paths above the recording redacted) — itself row VAL-DIAG-002.
- Emit a per-row structured pass/fail report (JSON + a human-readable summary). Include row id, tier, owner_on_fail, evidence paths, threshold values observed vs required, terminal event for exportId rows, and the linked source case from N-003/N-004/N-005/N-006. The report is the artefact T-010c consumes.
- Suite execution semantics: per N-008 §22, the smoke suite stops on the first must-pass red; per §23, the RC suite continues through reds and produces a full report.
- Manual rows are out of scope for the harness — it must SKIP them with a clear marker, not attempt to drive them. Manual rows are operator-driven per N-008 §4 and §19; the harness records their outcomes when a human marks them through a small operator endpoint (CLI flag or JSON ingest).

Deliverables:
- A repo-local runner (language and entrypoint TBD by implementer; recommend keeping it co-located with the helper crate so it can reuse the JSON-RPC types). MUST be invokable end-to-end with one command per suite: `runner smoke`, `runner rc`, `runner row <ID>`.
- A JSON schema for the per-row report.
- Coverage of every row in N-008 §22 (smoke), with the §6 thresholds wired through.
- Documentation for which rows are scripted-local (covered) vs manual (skipped) vs future-CI (deferred).

Out of scope (binding):
- Synthetic asset binaries — T-010b owns the L-* loads (N-008 §5).
- Execution against the M1..M4 hardware matrix — T-010c.
- Packaging concerns (sha256 sidecars, .deb Depends, electron-builder) — T-010d.
- Release execution — T-010e.
- Manual row procedures (portal pick UX, region overlay UX inspection, screensaver engagement) — operator-driven, the harness only ingests their result.
- L-AUDIO-SYNC (audio milestone, not v2.0.0 video-only GA).
- Windows hardware (W1 placeholder per N-008 §4).
- Any source-code changes to the helper or Electron app beyond what is strictly required to expose the JSON-RPC surface already locked in N-007.

Acceptance:
- The 18-row smoke suite from N-008 §22 runs end-to-end on M1, stops on first must-pass red, and produces a complete evidence bundle for every row that ran.
- Every scripted-local row in N-008 §§8–14 has a runnable harness implementation.
- The per-row report schema is documented and stable.
- Manual rows are explicitly skipped with a marker, not silently dropped.

No commits, tags, or publishes from this ticket.
title: v2.0.0 release: scripted-local runner harness
